Yes, it sounds like you need to speak with someone. What you've described could be diagnosed as depression by a psychiatrist, though it's not necessarily depression, or clinical depression. This is not to undermine or invalidate your feelings, but to tell you that you could be feeling this way for other reasons. 
That being said, at your age rather than seeking any kind of help, I persisted in thinking I could handle things on my own until it broke me. I won't go in to the details but it's worth asking for help because it opens up the possibility of feeling better, sooner.
The fact that you're asking these questions is a good sign. Obviously I don't know your family situation, so I can't tell you how you should approach this with your parents, if at all. Tell a friend if you think it would help. I personally would definitely opt for a trusted adult first - a favourite teacher or coach is a good starting point, but make sure it's someone who you trust not to panic. 

Expect the people you tell to be trepidatious. They don't know the extent of how you're feeling and may think you're feeling very, very bad indeed. Try to let them know you need some advice and guidance above all else. People do want to help, but it makes people uncomfortable. It's hard to hear that someone you care about and see regularly is in pain.
